content: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of vinorelbine by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, which is involved in its metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of voriconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Co-administration of cobicistat with voriconazole is not recommended unless the benefit-risk assessment justifies its use. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of warfarin through mechanisms involving the metabolism of its less potent R-enantiomer by CYP3A4, CYP1A2, and CYP2C19. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Monitor INR more frequently when co-administered with inhibitors of these isoenzymes, and adjust the warfarin dose as needed. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Reduce the zanubrutinib dose to 80 mg once daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Interrupt dosing as recommended for adverse reactions. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor, resume the previous zanubrutinib dose. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Reduce the zanubrutinib dose to 80 mg once daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Interrupt dosing as recommended for adverse reactions. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor, resume the previous zanubrutinib dose. Atazanavir and zidovudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of zuranolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Reduce the zuranolone dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Acetazolamide increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Acetazolamide also increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of alfentanil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Anastrozole increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of aliskiren by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of alosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of ambrisentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of amlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Amobarbital decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Anastrozole increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Aprepitant increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of armodafinil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, armodafinil decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of bosentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Budesonide decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Butabarbital decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Butalbital decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of cevimeline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Cortisone decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Cyclophosphamide increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cyclophosphamide also increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. Cyclosporine increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of dapsone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Darifenacin increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Dasatinib increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Dexamethasone decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. DHEA (herbal) increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of disopyramide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of docetaxel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of donepezil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of dutasteride by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of efavirenz by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, efavirenz decreases the levels of atazanavir through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. Co-administration is possible; refer to the atazanavir monograph for dosing information. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of eplerenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Eslcarbazepine acetate decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. However, packaging labeling states that etravirine and atazanavir/ritonavir can be co-administered without dose adjustments. The decrease in atazanavir levels is not clinically relevant when all three drugs are used. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of eucalyptus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of finasteride by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Fludrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of flutamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Cobicistat and ganaxolone interact by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Changes in ganaxolone exposures when co-administered with strong, moderate, or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors are not expected to be clinically significant. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Cobicistat and ixazomib interact by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. In clinical trials, co-administration of ixazomib with strong CYP3A inhibitors did not result in a clinically meaningful change in systemic exposure to ixazomib. Atazanavir and abacavir both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of abemaciclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase plasma levels of abemaciclib and its metabolites, necessitating dose reduction. If a patient taking abemaciclib discontinues a strong CYP3A inhibitor, increase the abemaciclib dose (after 3–5 half-lives of the inhibitor) to the dose used before starting the inhibitor. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of acalabrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Co-administration of acalabrutinib with strong CYP3A inhibitors should be avoided. If a strong CYP3A inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., up to 7 days), temporarily interrupt treatment with acalabrutinib. Atazanavir decreases the effects of acarbose through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. New onset or exacerbation of diabetes mellitus and hyperglycemia have been reported with protease inhibitors. Atazanavir increases the effects of acebutolol through pharmacodynamic synergism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. There is an increased risk of hypotension, bradycardia, AV block, and prolonged PR interval. Consider lowering the beta-blocker dose. Acetazolamide increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Acetazolamide also increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of adagrasib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration of adagrasib, a CYP3A4 substrate, with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided until adagrasib concentrations have reached steady-state (after ~8 days). If steady-state is not reached, concomitant use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors will increase adagrasib concentrations and the risk of its toxicities. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ado-trastuzumab emtansine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Atazanavir also increases levels of ado-trastuzumab emtansine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided. DM1, the cytotoxic component, is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4; strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase DM1 exposure and toxicity. Atazanavir decreases the effects of albiglutide through an unspecified mechanism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance have been associated with protease inhibitors. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of alfentanil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Atazanavir also increases the levels or effects of alfentanil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of alfuzosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Atazanavir also increases the levels or effects of alfuzosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the potential for increased alfuzosin concentrations, which can result in serious or life-threatening reactions such as hypotension. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of aliskiren by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of almotriptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely.
